text: Research tool: simulated results, not site predictions. Interpret with professional judgment. [Full disclaimer →]

**All model stages in the slip window** counts every recorded stage of every matching simulation inside your slip range — the measurements recorded at any stage within the range; with no slip window set, it counts every recorded stage. **One state per trial** counts only the last stage inside the window for each simulation — the measurements at the upper end of your range. With no slip window set, one state per trial is each simulation's final recorded state (approximately 5 m of slip). The two populations answer different questions and are never mixed.
Provisional data: scarp-dip values await a correction from the research group; the largest errors are concentrated in the Simple scarp types. Treat scarp-dip results as provisional.

These are statistics of the matching simulation records. The median is a typical result among them; the 84th percentile is a commonly used higher fractile in deterministic engineering practice. No statistic here is a recommended design value — selecting a design value remains the responsibility of the engineer of record.

You entered an anticipated vertical surface offset of {X} m. For each selected fault dip, this converts to the fault slip at depth shown here, using the ensemble's tested dip-specific relationship. The conversion assumes scarp height is approximately equal to vertical surface displacement — closest for Simple and Monoclinal scarps; Pressure Ridge scarps stand higher than the fault's vertical displacement, so the conversion tends to overstate slip where they dominate.
{Dip}°: converted slip ≈ {Y} m — beyond the modeled range (approximately 0–5 m). Coverage for this dip is partial; matching simulations exist only up to the modeled maximum (≈5 m of slip).
Enter the anticipated vertical surface offset (m) as a non-negative number — for example, 3 or 0.5. The value typed could not be read as one; the results still show the last valid scenario.
Field measurements (black): **analogous, not identical.** Field and simulated values represent related but non-identical quantities; each field source is named with its own measure.
Width overlays default to measurements under the paper's 50 m criterion; larger field widths may include distributed, multi-strand deformation the model does not represent.
Deformation-zone width measures the main modeled rupture zone. Real earthquakes can also produce separate deformation away from the main trace, which the model does not represent.
Only {N} valid measurements match this scenario — too few for a reliable distribution. Interpret with caution.
Fewer than 10 valid measurements match — too few for a reliable distribution. Showing the statistics table only; interpret with caution.
{X} simulation records match this scenario, but none has a valid {measurement} value — no distribution can be computed. The records appear in the excluded count of the statistics table.
Relaxing any one of {condition(s)} alone would produce matches.

Your window includes very small slip values, where automated measurements can be less reliable. The research group is reviewing measurement reliability at low slip; treat results near zero slip with extra caution.
